findings.title: Out-of-bounds read of one character past subject buffer end in scalar tail loop
findings.message: In the scalar 'remaining characters' tail loop of RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern, the loop is written as a C-style for loop where the initializer unconditionally dereferences `*block` before the loop condition `block < end` is evaluated: `for (SChar c = *block; block < end; c = *(++block))`. Because the initializer executes exactly once regardless of the loop condition, when the preceding SIMD block-processing loops have already advanced `block` to equal `end` (i.e., there are zero remaining scalar characters to process), this initializer still performs `*block`, reading one character past the end of the allocated subject string buffer. Although the loaded value is discarded (the loop body never executes since `block < end` is false), the read itself is undefined behavior and can be flagged by ASan/MSan or crash on the last page of a mapped buffer, constituting an out-of-bounds read vulnerability.
findings.suggestion: Do not dereference `*block` in the loop initializer before verifying `block < end`. Restructure the loop so the character is only loaded after the bounds check, e.g. move the load inside the loop body: `for (; block < end; ++block) { SChar c = *block; ... }`. This guarantees the pointer is never dereferenced once it has reached `end`.

ground_truth.root_cause: The scalar cleanup loop's for-statement puts a pointer dereference in the initializer clause, which is unconditionally evaluated once before the loop's controlling condition is checked. This violates the invariant that `block` must be checked against `end` before every dereference, allowing a read exactly at (one past) the end of the subject string's backing buffer when there are no trailing characters left to scan.
